chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Suwayd al-Qalanisi, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which Jihad is the most superior?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one whose horse is hamstrung and his blood is shed in the Way of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the most superior form of Jihad according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the pinnacle of Jihad as martyrdom, specifically highlighting the total sacrifice of one's resources (horse) and self (blood). This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *Jihad al-Akbar* through physical struggle and financial expenditure (*infal*) in the path of Allah, linking individual sacrifice directly to divine reward. The mention of the horse reflects the historical context of early Islamic warfare where cavalry was a primary means of exertion and status.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Suweyd Al qalanasy, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Which Jihad is the most superior?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one whose horse is hamstrung and his blood is shed in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from Suwayd al-Qalanisiy from Sama‘ah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Which kind of Jihad is more virtuous?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is the one in which the legs of one’s horse are cut off and his own blood is spilled for the cause of Allah.’”
